en: An off-the-shelf AI agent, planning on Kiln, was asked to buy a GPU hour from a cheaper seller that is not on the list. The vault on TRON refused, and recorded the stop on-chain.
Kiln explains it in plain words, shown only because it repeats the audit's verdict.
That agent is the OpenAI Agents SDK, unchanged, planning on Kiln. Our pass-through tied each of its payments to the Kiln call that asked for it.
This is the vault's public refusal record, SpendBlocked, with the receipt's fingerprint and the reason. Anyone can read it.
This is Spendline, a wallet and policy layer for an AI purchasing agent. A person draws the line. The agent only asks. The vault decides.
The person sets a budget, a per-payment cap, the sellers, and a deadline, one short step at a time.
Then signs it with the owner key, on their own machine. STOP is signed the same way.
The feed shows spending against the line, newest first: paid, or stopped with a reason.
Over budget once the fee is added: stopped on-chain.
The person can press STOP at any time. The next payment was stopped as PAUSED, on-chain.
A short time window: one payment inside it, then the same request after it closed. Stopped: deadline passed.
The audit, rebuilt from public records only: 38 receipts, 24 paid inside, 14 stopped, 0 problems.
The same check from the command line, with no key.

The same stock agent, with thinking switched off, bought a GPU hour and a Kiln credit. Sent the same request again, it was refused on-chain for both: it buys once, and the receipt keeps the person's words.
And a second witness. In plain words: Kiln's own logbook and the blockchain tell the same story for every AI call on the organizer's account, and each payment came 2 to 10 seconds after its call.
A teammate asks: was anything paid after I pressed STOP? Kiln picks the receipt. The verdict comes from the audit, never from the model.
On Friday, one command writes the statement: paid by seller, refused attempts, an intent flag, and a CSV for the accountant. Tune shows what next week's line would have done.
Efficiency: one LLM call per purchase attempt. No-think cut median output from 223 to 36 tokens. Energy is an estimate: 180 watts times measured time.
Spendline. Not an agent that can pay, but a payment that can prove it was allowed.
